identity.name: British Africa (remaining colonies)
alt_names: East Africa Protectorate (Wikipedia title of Cliopatria's row)

land.text: Britain's remaining colonies in Africa: Uganda, Kenya, Malawi (Nyasaland), Zambia (Northern Rhodesia), the Gambia, Zimbabwe (Southern Rhodesia), Botswana (Bechuanaland), Lesotho (Basutoland) and Swaziland; and five island groups the polygon also holds: Zanzibar and Pemba, Mafia Island, the Seychelles and Socotra

predecessors.note: A Cliopatria relabelling: the british-africa dossier records its row as ending in 1960 and this row starting in 1961. The shape resolves to Zambia (2,458 of 2,501 cells), Zimbabwe (1,282 of 1,304), Malawi (279 of 401), Botswana (1,991 of 2,010), Lesotho (104 of 111), Eswatini (54 of 62), the Gambia (36 of 43), Kenya (2,136 of 2,189) and Uganda (763 of 886), and almost nothing of Tanzania (18 of 3,227). The 13-part polygon also holds Zanzibar (Unguja) and Pemba, Mafia Island, Socotra and the Seychelles (areas read by the reviewer from the Cliopatria geometry; at the grid the gazetteer gives 4 cells for Zanzibar and Pemba, 1 for Mafia, 18 for Socotra and 0 for the Seychelles). Each is handled in keyframes 0-7 and the ledger.

keyframe_review.note: 2,676,386 km2 for 1961-1968. The 13-part Cliopatria polygon is NOT only the nine territories (the earlier 'cell for cell' reading was wrong). It holds the mainland blocks of Uganda, Kenya, Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe and Botswana, Lesotho, Swaziland and the Gambia, and also five islands that are not one of them (areas as read by the reviewer from the Cliopatria geometry): Zanzibar (Unguja, 2,306 km2) and Pemba (1,095 km2), a British protectorate until 10 December 1963 (ledger loss, counterpart sultanate-of-zanzibar); Mafia Island (866 km2), part of Tanganyika, lost at Tanganyika's independence on 9 December 1961 (ledger loss, counterpart tanzania); Socotra (5,563 km2), a protectorate of the Aden Protectorate in Arabia and so Asian, kept to South Yemen's independence on 30 November 1967 (ledger loss, counterpart people-s-democratic-republic-of-yemen); and the Seychelles (259 km2), British until 29 June 1976 and so in every keyframe to 1976. Three 58 km2 Lake Malawi islands lie inside Malawi. The gazetteer shows Zanzibar and Pemba 4 cells, Socotra 18 cells, Mafia 1 cell and the Seychelles 0 cells (too small for the grid; the country form gives one) inside the polygon. The infobox of the Wikipedia title Cliopatria gives (East Africa Protectorate) is a different entity: 696,400 km2 for 1904, a quarter of this shape, so the page cannot check the area. The shape holds whole only for 1961; each territory leaves on its independence date and the keyframes 1962-1967 shed the departures (land held at the end of each year).

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's second shape, 258.6 km2 for 1969-1972, is the Seychelles (bounding box 55.2-55.4 E, 4.6-4.8 S) and the same area as Cliopatria's Seychelles row from 1976. The same islands are already inside the 1961 shape (a 259 km2 polygon at 55.35 E 4.66 S), so there is no transfer in 1968: the Seychelles are held through 1961-1976 and the shape's years change from 1969-1972 to 1968-1976 (Swaziland leaves on 6 September 1968). At the 5-level grid it resolves to zero cells; the country form resolves to one. The table of the page lists the 'Crown Colony of the Seychelles' becoming independent on 29 June 1976.

ledger.note: 1961: Cliopatria continues British Africa as the remaining British colonies. The page dates no founding: 'Britain's remaining colonies in Africa, except for Southern Rhodesia, were all granted independence by 1968' (the page's own table puts the Seychelles in 1976). The shape is what remains of British Africa once Tanganyika (independent on 9 December 1961 on the page) and, per the british-africa dossier, Sierra Leone have their own Cliopatria rows; it also holds the island groups of Zanzibar and Pemba, Mafia, Socotra and the Seychelles (keyframe 0).

region.text: Mafia Island (Pwani Region, Tanzania), a separate 866 km2 polygon of the 1961 shape

ledger.note: 9 December 1961: Tanganyika becomes independent. Table: 'Tanganyika | Tanganyika Territory | 9 December 1961' (second table: 'Tanzania | 9 December 1961 | Independence of Tanganyika from the United Kingdom'). The page does not name Mafia Island; that it goes with Tanganyika is the researcher's reading (Mafia Island page: a district of Pwani Region, Tanzania, 'taken by British troops' on 12 January 1915). Cliopatria's Tanzania row starts in 1961.
9 October 1962: Uganda becomes independent. Table: 'Uganda | Protectorate of Uganda | United Kingdom | 9 October 1962' (self-government 'granted' on 1 March 1962).

region.text: the Zanzibar Archipelago, Unguja and Pemba

ledger.note: 10 December 1963: the British protectorate over Zanzibar ends and the Sultan rules a sovereign state. Table: 'Sultanate of Zanzibar | Sultanate of Zanzibar | 10 December 1963 | Jamshid bin Abdullah'. The Sultanate of Zanzibar dossier (another part) founds 1963-12 on the same land with counterpart british-colonial-empire; the counterpart should be this slug. Without this loss the islands were drawn twice from 1963 to 1965.
12 December 1963: Kenya becomes independent. Table: 'Kenya | Kenya Colony | 12 December 1963'; 'Kenyan independence was preceded by the eight-year Mau Mau rebellion.'
6 July 1964: Nyasaland becomes independent as Malawi. Table: 'Malawi | Nyasaland | 6 July 1964'.
24 October 1964: Northern Rhodesia becomes independent as Zambia. Table: 'Zambia | Northern Rhodesia | 24 October 1964'.
18 February 1965: the Gambia becomes independent. Table: 'The Gambia | Gambia Colony and Protectorate | 18 February 1965'.

11 November 1965: Southern Rhodesia declares independence unilaterally. Table: 'Zimbabwe | 11 November 1965 | Unilateral declaration of independence by Southern Rhodesia'; 'the 1965 Unilateral Declaration of Independence by the white minority'. The United Kingdom did not accept it: the page dates recognised independence as Zimbabwe on 18 April 1980. Recorded as a loss because the land left British control in fact; Cliopatria's Rhodesia row starts only in 1967.

30 September 1966: Bechuanaland becomes independent as Botswana. Table 2: 'Botswana | 30 September 1966 | Independence from the United Kingdom' (table 1 gives '30 September 1960 - 1966' for the Bechuanaland Protectorate; both end in 1966).
4 October 1966: Basutoland becomes independent as Lesotho. Table: 'Lesotho | United Kingdom Basutoland | 4 October 1966'.

region.text: Socotra (Mahra Sultanate of Qishn and Socotra, Aden Protectorate), a separate 5,563 km2 polygon of the 1961 shape

ledger.note: 30 November 1967: South Yemen becomes independent. 'the Federation and Protectorate of South Arabia were overthrown to become the People's Republic of Southern Yemen (PRSY) on 30 November 1967'. Socotra belonged to the Mahra Sultanate of Qishn and Socotra, under British protection from the treaty of 1886 (Aden Protectorate page: 'Beginning with a formal treaty of protection with the Mahra Sultanate of Qishn and Socotra in 1886'). Socotra is Asian: its place in this African set is an artifact of the Cliopatria polygon. That Socotra passes to the PRSY is the researcher's reading (the South Yemen page names the island only as a place where the National Liberation Front 'made headway'); Cliopatria's South Yemen row starts in 1969.

6 September 1968: Swaziland becomes independent. Table: 'Swaziland | United Kingdom Swaziland | 6 September 1968'; 'Eswatini | 6 September 1968 | Independence from the United Kingdom under the name Swaziland'. The Swaziland dossier records the same end of British protection as a vassal_end of the British colonial empire.

region.text: the Crown Colony of the Seychelles

ledger.note: 29 June 1976: the Seychelles become independent. Table: 'Seychelles | Crown Colony of the Seychelles | United Kingdom | 29 June 1976'.

29 June 1976: with the Seychelles, the last of Britain's remaining African colonies in this set becomes independent. Southern Rhodesia's independence had been declared unilaterally in 1965 and was recognised only on 18 April 1980 (the page).

certainty.note: Colonial boundaries with the neighbours; the pages opened do not delimit any of them. The Southern Rhodesian frontier is a de facto one after the unilateral declaration of independence of 1965.

notes: Page budget 2 of 2 originally; the repair run opened five more pages (Decolonisation of Africa again, Mafia Island, South Yemen, Aden Protectorate, Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland). THIS ROW IS A CLIOPATRIA ARTIFACT: the name and the Wikipedia link (East Africa Protectorate, 1895-1920, 696,400 km2) do not describe the 1961-1972 shapes. The first shape (2,676,386 km2, 1961-1968) is the remainder of British Africa: the nine territories (Uganda, Kenya, Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Botswana, Lesotho, Swaziland, the Gambia) PLUS five island groups that belong to none of them (corrected after review; the first draft wrongly called it cell for cell the nine territories): Zanzibar and Pemba (British protectorate to 10 December 1963; ledger loss to sultanate-of-zanzibar), Mafia Island (Tanganyika, lost 9 December 1961 to tanzania), Socotra (Aden Protectorate in Arabia, an Asian artifact, lost 30 November 1967 to people-s-democratic-republic-of-yemen) and the Seychelles (British to 29 June 1976, held in every keyframe). The second shape (258.6 km2, 1969-1972) is the Seychelles again. The 1968 'gain' of the Seychelles from british-colonial-empire in the first draft was deleted: the islands were in the shape from 1961 and the shape of british-colonial-empire for 1963-1968 does not hold them. The british-africa dossier (another af-08 part) reads the row as the continuation of British Africa and names this slug as its successor; the dossier is written as the remainder of British Africa ('British Africa (remaining colonies)') and the slug stays. Consequences for the rest of the group: (1) Cliopatria's independent rows start late (Uganda and Kenya 1963, Malawi, Zambia, the Gambia, Botswana, Lesotho and Rhodesia 1967) while independence came in 1962-1966, so each of those dossiers needs a keyframe back to its independence year or the land is blank in between. (2) Swaziland is drawn twice: this shape holds it to 1968 and the swaziland dossier draws it as its own polity for 1908-1968; the orchestrator must keep one. (3) sultanate-of-zanzibar founds 1963-12 with counterpart british-colonial-empire; the counterpart should be british-east-africa, or the islands are drawn twice 1963-1965 only if the other side is not fixed. (4) seychelles founds 1976-06 with counterpart kingdom-of-great-britain; the land comes from this slug. (5) people-s-democratic-republic-of-yemen (Cliopatria row 1969-1989, group me-10) must hold Socotra from 30 November 1967 or the island is blank 1967-1968. (6) The Seychelles polygon (259 km2) resolves to zero grid cells inside the 1961 shape and the country form gives one cell; Mafia (866 km2) gives one cell, Zanzibar and Pemba four, Socotra 18. (7) The Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland (1 August 1953 to 31 December 1963, a semi-independent federation under the Crown) moved no land out of British hands and is not an event here. (8) The founding in 1961 is a relabelling (confidence 1): the pages date no founding; the british-africa dossier ends its row in 1960. (9) Mauritius (12 March 1968) is not in the shape. Keyframes 1962-1967 hold the land at the end of each year. Gazetteer names needed: Mafia Island (place, 39.7 E 7.9 S), Socotra (place/admin1, 53.9 E 12.55 N); radii stand in.
